note: Track pentatonic-positions (guitar-scales), step 7: a run through positions 1, 2 and 3 with two slides, each crossing on its own first, then the run against a metronome and in a solo in a second key. missing: position-neck's cross shows one crossing between two positions, so the three-position run is told in the text over a plain three-position neck.

exercise.title: A run across three positions
exercise.why: Each position starts on the notes where the one below it ends, so two slides, each along one string, carry a run through three positions without a break.

cells.text:
The neck below shows only the crossing from position 1 to position 2 of A minor pentatonic. Climb position 1 from the low {{1}}, slide from {{4}} up to {{5}} on the G string, and finish the climb in position 2.
Come back down the same way.

Now the crossing from position 2 to position 3. Climb position 2, slide from {{5}} up to {{b7}} on the G string, and finish the climb in position 3.
This slide is one fret longer than the first, so listen for {{b7}} and stop the slide there.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Climb position 1 from the low {{1}}, slide from {{4}} to {{5}} on the G string, then from {{1}} to {{b3}} on the B string, and finish at the top of position 3. Come back down the same way, one note per beat.
Once every note lands on the click, try a faster stage. Use the Stage selector below to change the tempo, then press Play to start the metronome again.
If the slides smear at a stage, go back one and play only the two slides there.

Press Play below to start the backing track, which switches between Gm7 and Cm7. This is G minor pentatonic, two frets lower: improvise, and take the run across all three positions in the middle of a phrase.
When you change the key, the frets are new, but the slides are still {{4}} to {{5}} and {{1}} to {{b3}}.
